items.name: Two rackets (at least)
items.why: Strings break. Pros carry 6–8; you need two strung at the same tension.
items.tip: Keep them in a thermal bag; heat kills poly strings.

items.name: Overgrips
items.why: A fresh overgrip gives tack and absorbs sweat. Pros change them every set.
items.tip: Tacky (Wilson Pro, Yonex Super Grap) for dry hands; dry (Tourna Grip) for sweaty hands.

items.name: Tennis shoes for your surface
items.why: Hard-court shoes have durable outsoles; clay shoes have herringbone tread for sliding; grass shoes have nubs.
items.tip: Replace when the outsole tread under the big toe is gone.

items.name: Balls
items.why: Pressurised balls go dead in a few hours of hard play. Keep a fresh can for matches, old balls for serving practice.
items.tip: Pressureless balls for ball-machine and feeding drills.

items.name: Water and electrolytes
items.why: A three-set match in heat loses 2–3 litres of sweat.
items.tip: Drink at every changeover, not just when thirsty.

items.name: Towel
items.why: Dry the grip, the hands and the face.
items.tip: Two small towels beat one big one.

items.name: Spare strings
items.why: If you break strings often, carry a set so the stringer can restring overnight.
items.tip: Restring as many times a year as you play per week, minimum.

items.name: Vibration dampener
items.why: Removes the 'ping' sound. It does not reduce shock to the arm, whatever anyone says.
items.tip: Optional. Federer and Djokovic use none; Nadal and Agassi did.

items.name: Lead tape / tungsten tape
items.why: Customise weight and balance. 2 g at 12 o'clock adds plow-through.
items.tip: Add in small steps; swingweight changes fast.

items.name: Grip tape and finishing tape
items.why: Secure the end of the overgrip and replace worn base grips.
items.tip: A thinner base grip + overgrip gives the same feel as the stock grip.

items.name: Sunscreen, hat or visor, sunglasses
items.why: Four hours in the sun at a tournament is a serious dose.
items.tip: Sweat-resistant sunscreen; reapply at the changeover.

items.name: Wristbands and headband
items.why: Keep sweat off the grip and out of the eyes.
items.tip: Nadal and Federer wore them for a reason.

items.name: Spare shirt and socks
items.why: A dry shirt in the third set feels like a new match.
items.tip: Change socks too: blisters start in wet socks.

items.name: Energy
items.why: Bananas, energy gels, dates, dried fruit.
items.tip: Eat small amounts every few games in long matches.

items.name: Recovery kit
items.why: Foam roller, resistance band, massage ball.
items.tip: Five minutes of band work before play prevents most shoulder pain.

items.name: Medical kit
items.why: Blister plasters, athletic tape, anti-inflammatory gel, anti-chafe stick, ankle brace if you need it.
items.tip: Tape fingers that blister before you play, not after.

items.name: Ball machine or rebounder
items.why: Repetition builds technique faster than matches.
items.tip: Film yourself from the side to compare with the animations on this site.

items.name: Cones and targets
items.why: Hit to targets, not just over the net.
items.tip: Deep crosscourt targets first; angles later.

items.name: Jump rope and agility ladder
items.why: Footwork wins club matches.
items.tip: Five minutes before each session.

items.name: Phone tripod and a slow-motion app
items.why: Compare your contact point and finish to the pros.
items.tip: Film from behind and from the side.

items.name: A big tennis bag
items.why: 6-pack or 12-pack with a shoe compartment and a thermal pocket.
items.tip: Pack it the night before.
